## Notes — shared geometry and derivations

- **A320-200 (ceo) vs A320neo — same hull.** A single ACAP (AC_A320) covers both, with per-variant "ON A/C" blocks. The fuselage is identical; what changes is the engine (CFM56/V2500 → LEAP-1A/PW1100G), the pylon/nacelle and the wingtip (fence → sharklet). Model one master hull and parameterize engine + wingtip. The same logic holds for A321ceo vs A321neo (with the added caveat of the reconfigured doors on the A321neo-ACF, present in part of the LATAM fleet).
- **B767-300ER / -300F / -300BCF — same airframe.** All three share fuselage, wings, empennage and landing gear (a single D6-58328). Differences: the production -300F has no windows and has a forward left main cargo door; the BCF is a converted -300ER — it keeps plugged windows and the original passenger doors, gaining the freighter door in the -300F standard/position. A parametric -300ER generates all three via window/door plugs; for the BCF, LATAM Cargo photos fill in what the ACAP does not cover.
- **B787-8 vs B787-9 — same section, different lengths.** Fuselage cross-section, nose and wing are shared; the -9 is a stretch (+~6 m) with small door and gear differences. D6-58333 carries separate dimensioned 3-views for each — derive the -9 from the -8 (or vice versa) by parametric stretch validated against both 3-views.
- **A320 family: one ACAP per member.** The A319, A320 and A321 have separate documents (AC_A319, AC_A320, AC_A321) — AC_A320 does NOT cover the A319 or the A321. Each one carries its own 3-views in Ch. 2 and its footprint in Ch. 7.
- **Independent cross-check.** [OpenVSP Airshow](https://www.airshow.openvsp.org/) (A320, 767) provides clean parametric geometry to validate the curves extracted from the 600 dpi raster — a complement, never the final mesh. NASA 3D Resources does not have the LATAM types; ignore it.
- **URL stability.** Airbus moved the A320 family to the mediaassets CDN (URLs may rotate; stable entry point: the [Aircraft Characteristics page](https://www.aircraft.airbus.com/en/customer-care/fleet-wide-care/airport-operations-and-aircraft-characteristics/aircraft-characteristics)). Boeing moved the ACAPs to `content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/`; the old paths return 404. Every PDF exceeds what WebFetch can handle (>10 MB for the Boeing ones) — download via curl for the 600 dpi rasterization.
- **Licenses and future publication.** Nothing here blocks personal use, but GrabCAD (non-commercial, no redistribution), Sketchfab (a lottery of CC badges, several NC/ND) and viral GPL (FlightGear; A330 FG textures still awaiting release) contaminate future publication (CollabSoul video, portfolio). Rule: ACAP as the dimensional source of truth; open assets only as blocking/silhouette reference, never as a base mesh — in line with the project's fidelity directive (official brand SVG + livery applied as on the fleet).
